verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),path=require("path");const fail=(m)=>{console.error(m);process.exit(1)};const read=(f)=>fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8");const walk=(d)=>{if(!fs.existsSync(d))return[];return fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true}).flatMap((x)=>{const p=path.join(d,x.name);return x.isDirectory()?(x.name==="node_modules"?[]:walk(p)):[p]})};const v1=()=>walk("app/api/v1").filter((f)=>/route\.ts$/.test(f));const v1src=()=>v1().map(read).join("\n");const t=read("app/terms/page.tsx");if(!/objectionable/i.test(t)||!/tolerance/i.test(t))fail("the terms carry no zero-tolerance clause for objectionable content and abusive members (App Store 1.2)");const g=["app/guidelines/page.tsx","app/community-guidelines/page.tsx"].find((f)=>fs.existsSync(f));if(!g)fail("there is no community guidelines page");const s=v1src();if(!/blockUser/.test(s))fail("a native client cannot block a member");if(!/report/i.test(s))fail("a native client cannot report content");console.log("ok")'

append.detail: 2026-10-06: the terms carry a zero-tolerance clause (24-hour review, removal and suspension); /guidelines is the public rule set, linked from the terms, the report dialog, both footers, the nav registry and the sitemap; POST /api/v1/reports runs the web's reportContent as the caller and POST/DELETE /api/v1/blocks call lib/blocking. The wording is a draft for the owner's review, not legal advice (the terms banner says so). Tested in app/api/v1/reports/route.test.ts.
